text.p: British retailer Allders Plc on Tuesday said it was looking for opportunities to expand its department store business, but was in no rush to make more acquisitions.

Chief executive Harvey Lipsith said the group, which in September bought eight department stores from Owen Owen Plc for 23.6 million stg, was always looking at what was available, but nothing was very far advanced.
He said in a telephone interview the group was busy converting the Owen Owen stores into the Allders format. "We've got enough on our hands for a little while," he said.

Allders has expanded from 19 stores to 30 in two years and is entirely focused on department store retailing since the sale of its Allders International duty free business to Swissair in June for 160 million stg.

When asked if the group might be interested in any stores put up for sale by loss-making rival House of Fraser, Lipsith said the company was not looking specifically at House of Fraser sites, since he said it was not clear which ones were for sale.
He said Allders would spend about 15 million stg on the Owen Owen stores over two years. All eight stores now have the Allders name and 40 percent of the space has been refitted.
Over the next couple of years the group expects to spend about 30 million stg on new stores and existing stores.
Lipsith said its new "Allders at Home" store in Basingstoke in southern England, which opened in September was performing above expectations.
The chief executive said group margins were up by half a percentage point in the year to 35 percent.
The sale of the duty free business left Allders with net cash of some 87 million stg at the year end, but in September it paid out 50 million to shareholders through a special dividend.
Lipsith said the group would stay ungeared or marginally geared for the next couple of years.
Profits in the year to September 30 rose to 40.4 million stg from 23.5 million, but the profit figure included a 33.2 million stg profit on the sale of Allders International.
